nextStoryContext: US-015 added the single-supervisor concurrency guard. src/supervisor/lock.ts exports acquireSupervisorLock(pid, project, io) and parseLockInfo over an injected LockIo (read/write/remove/pidAlive/clock + optional logEvent). Behavior: no/unparseable lock -> take it; lock owned by a DIFFERENT live pid -> { acquired: false, holderPid }; dead pid -> emit a 'stale-lock' WorkerEvent (events.ts WorkerEventKind gained 'stale-lock', uuid 'supervisor') then take over. Wired in src/commands/next.ts (NOT runSupervisor, which stays pure): acquire right after the worker-pane check and before the state-file write; on conflict printError('supervisor already running (pid=N)') + return 1; release at every terminal return AND via one process-wide SIGINT/SIGTERM handler (installShutdownHandler, module-singleton currentLockRelease). New NextOptions: lockPath, acquireLock, onShutdown (all injectable for tests). logEvent is now created once near the top of runNext and shared by the guard + supervisor. PID liveness reuses isPidAlive from resume.ts. Lock file .claude/.cam-supervisor.lock is gitignored. Remaining non-operator stories: US-016 (rate-limit handling via src/retry/*), US-017 (recovery runbook in docs/). US-018 requires:operator (real E2E). NOTE: implemented directly in a Claude Code session (no live -L cam worker pane in this checkout), not via a dispatched headless worker; no .cam-worker-US-015.session marker exists.

officialDocsValidated.summary: US-015 is pure TypeScript over node:fs and process.kill(pid, 0). No new npm packages. The signal-0 liveness probe is reused from the in-repo isPidAlive (src/commands/resume.ts), already validated in prior work; no external doc fetch warranted.
